minutes.headline: Sewer Commission discussed an expected rate increase and capital plan but took no rate vote; the assistant hire is on hold.
minutes.summary: The commission reviewed the business manager's forecast spreadsheets covering the FY23 year-end estimate, a five-year rate and capital scenario tool, and a Fitchburg rate increase. Members agreed a rate increase is coming but deferred any number until Leominster's position is known. The assistant business manager hire is stalled over the union's 24-hour minimum. The meeting adjourned by roll call.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission set no rate increase figure and will wait for Leominster's position before choosing one.
Members agreed a rate increase is coming, after the business manager reported Fitchburg's increase as a percentage each year over five years.
The assistant business manager hire is on hold while the business manager and the union and town administrator try to cut the position to 19 hours.
The business manager's FY23 year-end estimate shows revenue under expectations and capital spending needed, so the usual surplus is not expected.
The commission took no votes; the meeting ended by roll call, and the next meetings were noted for May 9, May 30 and June 13.

why_it_matters: Sewer rates are charged to users, so a decision on the size of the increase is still ahead and will depend on what Leominster and Fitchburg charge.
The surplus normally returned to retained earnings is expected to be smaller this year, and the unfilled assistant position leaves the staffing question open.
watch_next: Sewer Commission meetings on May 9, May 30 and June 13, where a rate figure may be taken up once Leominster's position is known.
The dates Leominster proposes for a daytime meeting, which the business manager is to send to members.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the main figures: Fitchburg's 7% for five years, the $17K surplus, the 12% scenario with its $419K draw, and the rate increase being left open. Ours has much more budget-worksheet detail, and the official minutes add the tabled prior minutes. The one conflict to check is the Assistant Business Manager. Ours records a hold until the hours are cut to 19, and the official minutes only show an unfilled position offsetting payroll. Dave MacDonald is also marked absent officially but "possibly joining later" in ours.
